sandhi.note: As in 3.41: -aḥ before e loses its visarga, the vowels stay apart; a + a → ā.

morph.note: Present middle participle (-मान) of the divādi root √युध् (stem युध्य-). In 3.15 the Gita Press prints the same form with a doubled stop, युद्ध्यमानौ; here it is printed युध्यमानो.

Absolutive of √छिद् (d → t before -त्वा). Its agent is the Goddess, who appears in the instrumental as agent of the passive निपातितः: an absolutive shares the agent of the main action even when that agent is in the instrumental.

mantras.anvaya: अर्धनिष्क्रान्तः एव युध्यमानः असौ महासुरः तया देव्या महासिना शिरः छित्त्वा निपातितः।
mantras.anvaya_en: Passive construction: subject असौ महासुरः, predicate निपातितः, agent तया देव्या; the absolutive छित्त्वा shares that agent.
mantras.lit: That great asura, still only half emerged (and) fighting, was struck down by that Goddess, (she) having cut off (his) head with (her) great sword.
mantras.tr: Still only half emerged, still fighting, the great demon was struck down by the Goddess, who cut off his head with her great sword.
mantras.tr_note: The Sanskrit is passive; the English keeps the passive for the asura and turns the absolutive into a relative clause for the Goddess.

comm.t: The death of Mahiṣa. He fights to the end (युध्यमानः), half out of the buffalo; the Goddess beheads him with the great sword. The head she was about to cut off in 3.30 falls now. Among her gifts in chapter 2 the sword came from Kāla (कालश्च दत्तवान् खड्गम्, 2.24).
A modern reading: the end comes not when the asura is strongest but in the middle of a change he cannot complete — still fighting, still half of what he was.

sandhi.note: Before s the visarga of जग्मुः may stand (the optional s-assimilation is not written); -āḥ before the voiced d loses its visarga.

samasa.alt: Also read as a compound of the indeclinable हाहा (an exclamation) with the participle कृत, like अलंकृत: ‘(an army) lamenting’. The sense is the same.

samasa.sense: all the companies of the gods

morph.note: Perfect of √नश्: reduplication न-, vṛddhi of the root a in the third singular.
Perfect third plural of √गम्: reduplication ज- (g → j) and loss of the root a before the vowel ending (ज-ग्म्-उः). प्रहर्षं जग्मुः ‘went to joy’ is the regular idiom for ‘became joyful’.

mantras.anvaya: ततः हाहाकृतं तत् सर्वं दैत्यसैन्यं ननाश। सकलाः देवतागणाः च परं प्रहर्षं जग्मुः।
mantras.lit: Then that whole army of the Daityas, crying out in woe, perished; and all the hosts of the gods went to supreme joy.
mantras.tr: Then the whole demon army, wailing, was destroyed, and all the hosts of the gods were filled with the greatest joy.

comm.t: With its leader dead the asura army collapses, and the gods rejoice — the ‘roaring’ the Goddess promised in 3.38. A textual note: the Purāṇa recension in GRETIL’s Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa carries further verses at this point that the Gita Press Saptaśatī does not (recorded in the edition’s recension notes); the recited 700-mantra text, followed here, passes straight to the gods’ praise (3.44).

sandhi.note: After ai the visarga appears as r before a voiced sound; so जगुर्गन्धर्व- (after u).
-aḥ before n → -o; visarga before c → ś; a + a → ā.
Inside the compound the final s of the stem अप्सरस् becomes o before the voiced g, as -aḥ does between words; च + अ- before it gives चा- (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः, 6.1.101).

samasa.vigraha: महान्तः च ते ऋषयः च, तैः

samasa.sense: the chiefs of the celestial musicians

morph.note: Perfect third plural of √स्तु: the reduplicated syllable keeps only the stop (तु-), the root’s s becomes ṣ after the u of the reduplication (ष्टु, with t → ṭ beside ṣ), and u → uv before the vowel ending.
Perfect third plural of √गै, treated as गा: ज-ग्-उः, the ā lost before the vowel ending (like ययुः, 3.27).
Perfect third plural of √नृत्: reduplication न-, the root ṛ unchanged in the weak (plural) forms.

mantras.anvaya: सुराः दिव्यैः महर्षिभिः सह तां देवीं तुष्टुवुः। गन्धर्वपतयः जगुः, अप्सरोगणाः च ननृतुः।
mantras.anvaya_en: Three clauses, each with its own subject and perfect verb: the gods praise, the Gandharvas sing, the Apsarases dance.
mantras.lit: The gods, together with the heavenly great seers, praised that Goddess; the lords of the Gandharvas sang, and the troupes of Apsarases danced.
mantras.tr: The gods, with the heavenly great sages, sang the Goddess’s praise; the Gandharva lords sang and the Apsarases danced.

comm.t: The chapter closes in celebration: praise, song and dance. तुष्टुवुः ‘they praised’ is taken up in the next chapter, where the gods led by Indra sing their hymn to the Goddess (तां तुष्टुवुः, 4.2).
In the Gita Press pāṭha this is the last mantra of the third chapter and carries the closing bīja ॐ, which belongs to the recitation, not to the verse.
